questions.question: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vitamin D**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets** is a condition that affects bone development in children. It causes the bones to become soft and weak, which can lead to bone deformities.
 
• The primary cause of rickets is a **deficiency of vitamin D**.
 
• Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the diet, which are critical for healthy bone formation.
 
• Without sufficient vitamin D, the body cannot properly regulate calcium and phosphate levels, leading to the symptoms of rickets.
 
• Common sources of vitamin D include exposure to sunlight, which triggers vitamin D production in the skin, and dietary sources such as fatty fish, liver, and fortified foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rickets can also be caused by genetic factors, certain medical conditions, or malabsorption disorders that affect the body's ability to process vitamin D.
 
• Preventing rickets involves ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D through diet and supplementation, as well as sensible sun exposure.
 
• Treatment for rickets typically includes vitamin D and calcium supplements, and in severe cases, corrective surgery may be required to address bone deformities.
 
• Public health measures, such as fortifying foods with vitamin D, have been effective in reducing the incidence of rickets in many parts of the world.

• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**

• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The allocation of Lok Sabha seats is periodically revised based on population changes reflected in the decennial census.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a directive principle of international peace and security?

options.text: Promotion of international peace and security
Create opportunities of employment for foreigners
Respect for international laws and treaty obligations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Create opportunities of employment for foreigners**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The directive principles of international peace and security are guidelines for the government to follow in order to promote global harmony and stability.
 
• **Encourage settlements of international disputes**, **Promotion of international peace and security**, and **Respect for international laws and treaty obligations** are recognized as directive principles aimed at fostering peaceful international relations.
 
• **Create opportunities of employment for foreigners** is not a directive principle of international peace and security. It is more related to economic policies and employment strategies rather than international peace and security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The directive principles of state policy in India are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution of India. They serve as guidelines to the central and state governments of India to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• These principles are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, aiming to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The directive principles related to international peace and security emphasize the importance of maintaining friendly relations with other nations and adhering to international laws and treaties.

questions.question: Which glands help in digestion in the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gastric glands**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gastric glands** are responsible for aiding digestion in the stomach.
 
• These glands secrete gastric juice, which contains hydrochloric acid and digestive enzymes such as pepsin.
 
• The hydrochloric acid creates an acidic environment that helps in breaking down food, and the enzyme pepsin breaks down proteins into peptides.
 
• Gastric glands are located in the lining of the stomach and play a crucial role in the digestive process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gastric glands** are composed of different types of cells, including parietal cells, chief cells, and mucous cells.
 
• **Parietal cells** secrete hydrochloric acid, which helps in killing bacteria and activating pepsinogen to pepsin.
 
• **Chief cells** produce pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of pepsin.
 
• **Mucous cells** secrete mucus to protect the stomach lining from the harsh acidic environment.
 
• Malfunction or diseases affecting the gastric glands can lead to digestive issues such as ulcers and gastritis.

questions.question: In the context of British rule in India, who among the following Governor-Generals created a professional cadre of company servants making provisions for them for generous salaries?

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was the Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793.
 
• He is known for creating a professional cadre of company servants and making provisions for them for generous salaries.
 
• His reforms, known as the **Cornwallis Code**, included measures to curb corruption among company officials by paying them adequately.
 
• Lord Cornwallis also introduced significant judicial and administrative reforms in British India.

• **Lord Mayo** and **Lord Dalhousie** also served as Governor-Generals but were known for other reforms and administrative measures.
 
• The Cornwallis Code also included the introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, which restructured land revenue collection.
 
• His tenure marked the beginning of a more systematic and bureaucratic approach to governance in British India.

questions.question: McMahon Line is the boundary line between India and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The McMahon Line is the boundary line between India and **China**.
 
• It was established as part of the Simla Convention signed in 1914 between British India and Tibet, which was not recognized by China at that time.
 
• The line is named after Sir Henry McMahon, who was the chief negotiator from the British side.
 
• The McMahon Line runs through the eastern sector of the India-China border, which is disputed by China.
 
• It is a major point of contention in the border disputes between India and China, leading to several conflicts, including the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Simla Convention was an attempt to settle the boundaries between British India and Tibet, and to establish Tibet as an autonomous region under Chinese suzerainty.
 
• China did not accept the Simla Convention, arguing that Tibet was not a sovereign entity and hence had no authority to sign treaties.
 
• The McMahon Line has been a flashpoint in India-China relations, with both countries strengthening their military presence along the border.
 
• Despite the disputes, the McMahon Line is currently the de facto border in the eastern sector between India and China.
 
• Efforts have been made through diplomatic channels to resolve the boundary issues, but a final settlement has not yet been reached.
